accuracy.reason: All nine objectives accurately cover embedded persistence/local fit, affinity/STRICT/constraints, configured ACID, single-writer busy handling, rollback/WAL/checkpoint behavior, plans/indexes, backups/migrations and workload choice. SQLite primary pages support the scoped claims.

evidence.quote: SQLite changes where the database runs. You still have a relational database.

mechanisms.reason: Process/file access, concurrent writer contention, stable WAL reader state, checkpoint delay and missing main-file backup state have clear causes. Diagrams preserve in-process versus server boundary, one writer, WAL/checkpoint and query/index flow.

evidence.quote: Choose based on the workload and access pattern, not whether the project is small or serious.

coherence.reason: Each declared prerequisite precedes use: embedded/locality to rules/transactions, then contention/WAL, query plans, operation and choice. Learner applies the full stack without requiring a quiescent-copy procedure as the sole backup option.

evidence.quote: Decide which flexibility you want and which rules the database must enforce.

decisions.reason: Choices weigh local simplicity against shared-network access and competing writes; short transactions/retries mitigate but do not remove limits. Index cost, filesystem/flush guarantees and tested historical recovery remain explicit responsibilities.

evidence.quote: A successful commit and protection against every kind of failure are not interchangeable promises.

clarity.reason: Terms including affinity, STRICT, busy, journal, checkpoint and migration are defined. Diagrams agree with prose. Shared renderer/CSS inspected, not executed. Learner appropriately marks optional numeric thresholds and implementation procedures unspecified.

evidence.quote: Measure write contention and transaction duration, not just the number of users.

outcomes.reason: All six criteria satisfied across slides 1-2/8-9: learner traces in-process SQL/file persistence, relational features, local/single-host uses, multi-server access difficulty and no user-count/sync guarantee. Operational responsibilities appear in its query/choice answers and are accepted across the whole stack.

All eight criteria satisfied: actual learner explains affinity/storage classes/STRICT ANY, explicit required constraints and per-connection verified foreign keys, ACID/commit/rollback and correct logic, configured flush/storage durability and external-effect boundary; slides 3-4/6 support it.

All eight criteria satisfied: learner separates connections/readers from one writer, busy contention/short transactions/bounded retry/failure, rollback undo versus WAL append, stable readers/checkpoint growth and same-host limits. Slides 5-6 support each mechanism.

All eight criteria satisfied: learner derives owner/time index from taught columns/order, uses plan/measurement and scan/cost caveats, assigns permissions/capacity/migration/recovery duties, explains missing WAL state and selects supported consistent backup plus tested usability. Quiescent copying is an alternative, not a required second recipe.

All four criteria satisfied: learner conditionally accepts local short writes and evaluates client-server for sustained shared multi-server writes, retaining explicit rules/transactions/plans/backups and measuring contention/duration/query/recovery instead of arbitrary thresholds.

sourceChecks.claim: Live SQLite appropriate-uses contrasts local application storage with client-server shared repository and explicitly allows single-host application-server use.
Live appropriate-uses checklist chooses by direct access locality and writers able to take turns, not a universal human-user cutoff.

Live STRICT Tables confirms ordinary lossless-conversion affinity versus STRICT and ANY; Foreign Key Support followup explicitly requires enabling/verifying each connection. Constraints remain explicit.

Live PRAGMA synchronous documents power-loss durability differences by mode and filesystem, including WAL NORMAL loss risk; isolation page confirms normal committed visibility and journaling transaction boundaries.
Live Isolation explicitly permits multiple connections/processes but serializes writers, describes locking and snapshot upgrade busy behavior; bounded wait cannot create writer capacity.

Live WAL sections 2-3 describe original-page rollback versus appended changes, checkpoints, stable readers and single writer; same-host shared-memory condition and reader-induced checkpoint starvation support limits.
Live Query Planning describes cost-based scans, multi-column search/sort and index paths; table/query shape determines benefit, not mere locality.

Live Backup API guarantees consistent snapshot after supported backup completion; WAL page confirms committed changes outside main file. ALTER TABLE primary followup documents table-rebuild path for other changes. Restore testing is justified operational validation.
Live appropriate-uses explicitly recommends client/server when many writers cannot queue/take turns and permits local storage behind application server; no distributed WAL guarantee.
